sections.title: Rose genus
sections.text: Rosa is a large genus of deciduous or evergreen shrubs and climbers, with prickly stems, pinnate leaves, and usually five-petalled flowers. Species vary greatly in stature and flower and hip size, so this generic plate cannot be assigned a reliable height or width.

sections.title: Flowers and hips
sections.text: After pollination, the flower base develops into a fleshy hip containing the true fruits (achenes). Petals and ripe hips of many rose species are eaten or used in preserves and drinks, but this should not be generalized to every ornamental cultivar or pesticide-treated plant. The stiff hairs around the achenes can irritate the mouth and digestive tract and should be removed during food preparation.
